title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: People living longer
sections.summary: The number of people living to 100 and beyond has doubled over the last decade, rising from 65 in the 1960s to more than 86 now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: From what was 65 in the 1960s, to now, more than 86, according to BBC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The number of people living to 100 years and beyond has also doubled over the last decade.

sections.label: Oxford index and OECD report
sections.summary: The Blavatnik School of Government index rates public services in four areas, and an OECD report cited Singapore's well-defined budget framework and fiscal discipline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This is the index produced by the Blavatnik School of Government at the University of Oxford, which rates public services in four areas: strategy and leadership, public policies, national delivery and people and processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: However, in the interest of guillotine time, I would just mention one more international accolade that Singapore has just received last month, which cited that the Government of Singapore as having, "a well-defined budget framework with clear fiscal objectives".

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This is the report by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) on "Budgeting in Singapore", which also mentioned Singapore as having an international reputation for fiscal discipline in budgeting and policies that has help ensure long-term fiscal sustainability.

sections.label: HDB resale prices rising
sections.summary: By the end of 2025, HDB resale prices are set to rise for a record 23 quarters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By the end of 2025, Housing and Development Board (HDB) resale prices are set to rise for a record 23-quarters.

sections.label: Cumulative HDB resale increase
sections.summary: The projected 2025 increase means resale HDB prices would have risen by a cumulative 58% since early 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The projected increase for 2025 means that resale HDB prices would have risen since early 2020 by a cumulative 58%.

sections.label: HDB resale price climb 2024
sections.summary: Despite expectations of slower price rises in 2024, HDB resale prices climbed 9.7% that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Based on what the Minister said, a reasonable expectation would be for price rises to have slowed down further in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But then, the news in January this year was that in 2024, HDB resale prices climbed the steep 9.7%.

sections.label: Concern over HDB land pricing
sections.summary: With resale flat prices up 58% from 2020 to 2024, there is concern over whether land for HDB BTO flats is priced sustainably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With a 58% increase in resale flat prices from 2020 to 2024, there is inevitably a serious concern about whether land for HDB BTO flats is priced sustainably, or if ever-growing subsidies are going to be needed in future to make HDB flats affordable.

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme extensions and PWCS
sections.summary: The Wage Credit Scheme, started in 2013 as a temporary three-year measure, has been repeatedly extended and expanded into PWCS with $9 billion allocated from 2022 to 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the Wage Credit Scheme (WCS) was started in 2013 as a temporary three-year measure to support PWM, it has been repeatedly extended and expanded.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This has now evolved into PWCS with an allocation of $9 billion from 2022 to 2026, to this temporary measure first introduced 12 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, PWCS co-funding increased from plan levels of 30% to 50% to 45% to 75% in 2022 to 2023.

sections.label: Fiscal headroom and spending to 2030
sections.summary: Fiscal headroom will shrink as expenditure is projected to rise while revenues remain uncertain, but projected spending up to 2030 is affordable due to fiscal measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Chairman, our fiscal headroom will get smaller as Government expenditure is projected to increase while our revenues remain uncertain in light of the status of BEPS 2.0 and heightened geopolitical and trade tensions affecting investment returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We can afford the projected level of spending up to 2030 thanks to sound and timely fiscal measures made.

sections.label: GIC annual performance figures
sections.summary: Unlike Temasek Holdings, GIC does not share annual performance figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Unlike Temasek Holdings, GIC does not even share annual performance figures.

sections.label: IRAS GST display concession for hotels and F&B
sections.summary: IRAS grants hotels and F&B outlets an administrative concession to display prices ex-GST if they impose a service charge, unlike other retail sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Currently, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) grants hotels and F&B outlets an administrative concession which allows them to display prices ex-GST if they also impose a service charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This differs from other retail sectors, where the price displays must include GST.

sections.label: Reviewing GST concession and CDC Vouchers
sections.summary: The speaker urges IRAS to review the concession and require all-inclusive price displays, and suggests using CHAS, Merdeka and Pioneer schemes instead of CDC Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the interest of ensuring a level playing field between F&B operators and improve consumers' dining experience by having greater price transparency, I urge IRAS to review this concession and to require the display of all-inclusive prices as I believe the overall real benefits to the public outweigh any perceived cost to businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In my 2024 and the recent 2025 Budget debate speeches, I highlighted that while the CDC Vouchers Scheme has provided some support for Singaporeans amidst the high cost of living, the support rendered is broad-based, with low-income households receiving the same payout as that of a millionaire CEO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In lieu of the CDC Vouchers Scheme, the Government could leverage the existing Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), Merdeka Generation and Pioneer Generation schemes to provide discounts for cardholders at merchants, hawkers and supermarkets that currently accept CDC Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The rebate provided could vary based on the colour of one's CHAS card, with blue CHAS cardholders receiving the largest discount quantum, along with Merdeka and Pioneer Generation cardholders.

sections.label: Support for low to middle-income households
sections.summary: Through this scheme, greater support will be rendered to low to middle-income households and residents compared to high net worth individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Through this scheme, greater support will be rendered to low to middle-income households and residents compared to high net worth individuals.

sections.label: Philanthropy Tax Incentive Scheme
sections.summary: Singapore introduced the Philanthropy Tax Incentive Scheme, offering tax benefits for qualifying overseas donations to family offices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: More recently, as part of our ambition to be Asia's philanthropic hub, Singapore introduced the Philanthropy Tax Incentive Scheme (PTIS), which offers tax benefits for qualifying overseas donations to family offices.

sections.label: Tax incentives for grantmaking
sections.summary: Existing tax incentives for philanthropy, such as PTIS and the IPC scheme, apply only to grantmaking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, existing tax incentives for philanthropy, such as PTIS and the Institution of a Public Character (IPC) scheme, apply only to grantmaking.

sections.label: India corporate social responsibility policy
sections.summary: India requires companies of a certain size to contribute 2% of net earnings to corporate social responsibility, and Singapore can learn from this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For instance, India introduced a mandatory policy requiring companies of a certain size to contribute 2% of their net earnings to corporate social responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore can learn from this, not through regulation but by establishing a corporate social impact benchmark that sets an aspirational standard for corporate giving, a desired philanthropic spending target that would encourage businesses to integrate social impact into their strategies.

sections.label: Measuring and streamlining process
sections.summary: MOF is asked whether it can, with other Ministries, measure and streamline this process to minimise delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To maximise impact and efficiency, can MOF, in collaboration with other Ministries, measure and streamline this process to minimise delays and ensure that promising initiatives are not hindered by bureaucracy?

sections.label: Simplifying regulatory requirements
sections.summary: MOF is asked what steps it is taking to simplify regulatory requirements, manage compliance costs and improve ease of business transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What steps is MOF taking to simplify regulatory requirements, manage compliance costs and improve overall ease of business transactions with Government agencies?

sections.label: Social value in procurement
sections.summary: MOF is urged to consider formalising the embedding of social value into the Government procurement framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the same vein, I would like to urge MOF to consider formalising the embedding of social value into Government procurement framework.

sections.label: Social value in procurement
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Minister would embed social value objectives such as local hiring and training into Government procurement.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They need a supportive environment to acquire and sharpen their edge to compete in a fast-changing landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, would the Minister consider strengthening the Government's positive impact by embedding social value objectives, such as supporting hiring of locals, upscaling and training into the Government procurement framework?

sections.label: Change management for startups
sections.summary: A question asks what change management the Government is doing to upscale and change mindsets of Ministries and agencies on working with startups.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: What form of change management is the Government doing to upscale and change mindsets of Government Ministries and agencies on working with startups?

sections.label: Tender Lite SME contracts
sections.summary: A question asks for more information on how many Tender Lite contracts have been awarded to SMEs since April 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Tender Lite was introduced by MOF and implemented in April 2024 to make it easier for companies, especially SMEs, to bid for Government contracts higher than $90,000 and not more than $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: To date, can more information be shared on how many Tender Lite contracts have been awarded to SMEs since the implementation?

sections.label: On-time payments to suppliers
sections.summary: A question asks MOF for an update on the percentage of payments made on time to suppliers in Government tenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can MOF provide an update on what percentage of payments are made on time to suppliers who participate in Government tenders?

sections.label: Pro-Enterprise Rules Review Committee
sections.summary: The Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review was formed in April 2024, and IRAS will extend the GST charging grace period.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Inter-Ministerial Committee for Pro-Enterprise Rules Review, led by Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, was formed in April 2024 to further enhance regulatory efficiency and reduce compliance costs for businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: First, IRAS will extend the grace period for businesses to begin charging GST from one month to two months.

sections.label: GST grace period extension
sections.summary: The change gives SMEs more time to prepare, takes effect 1 July 2025 and benefits 1,500 businesses every year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The change will give SMEs more time to prepare.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It will take effect from 1 July 2025 and benefit 1,500 businesses every year.

sections.label: ACRA streamlined exemption process
sections.summary: ACRA streamlined the process so non-listed companies need not seek exemption if all shareholders consent, saving $200 in fees for about 1,500 companies yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: ACRA has recently streamlined this process such that non-listed companies do not need to seek exemption, as long as consent from all shareholders is sought.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This will reduce administrative burden and save companies $200 in application fees and we expect around 1,500 companies to benefit every year.

sections.label: Government savings and service satisfaction
sections.summary: The four-in-one East Coast Integrated Depot saved $2 billion and 44 hectares, ServiceSG satisfaction exceeded 90%, and joint budgets and a 2022 transformation budget were created.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, we saved $2 billion and 44 hectares of land with the four-in-one East Coast Integrated Depot, which combines three Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) depots and one bus depot.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Citizen satisfaction across ServiceSG centres was consistently above 90% for the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We use joint budgets for issues that straddle multiple agencies, to streamline efforts, check against resource duplication and enhance accountability for shared outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We also created the whole-of-Government Public Service Transformation Budget in 2022.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme cessation
sections.summary: Ms He Ting Ru asked about the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, which is currently due to cease in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Ms He Ting Ru asked about the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It is currently due to cease in 2026.

sections.label: Net Investment Returns Contribution share
sections.summary: The Net Investment Returns Contribution now accounts for about a fifth of annual government revenue.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) now accounts for about a fifth of our annual government revenue.

sections.label: Reserves disclosure and GIC assets
sections.summary: Reserves management framework and governance are published on the MOF website, but GIC's assets under management remain undisclosed to avoid revealing reserves size.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We have also published information on our reserves management framework and governance on the MOF website.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It is only the size of GIC's assets under management that remains undisclosed, as this would reveal the size of our reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: And just as our defence forces do not reveal the full extent of our military capabilities, it is not in Singapore's national interest to disclose the full size of our reserves.

sections.label: Assessing entities by mandates
sections.summary: Entities are assessed on mandates and long-term performance, considering portfolio diversification and risk adjusted returns relative to risk taken.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Instead, we assess our entities based on their mandates and performance over the long term and consider factors, such as diversification of portfolios and risk adjusted returns which measure investment returns relative to the risk taken.

sections.label: CDC Voucher Scheme eligibility debate
sections.summary: A speaker questions whether the call is to stop CDC Vouchers completely or limit them to low-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And then, he went into a scheme where you would have benefits according to CHAS.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: But what I was not sure was whether he was calling for the CDC Voucher Scheme to be stopped completely, or whether he is saying that the CDC Voucher Scheme should be limited only to the low-income, because in the gist of the cut that he filed, he had said that rather than giving CDC Vouchers to all, we should return to the roots of CDC Vouchers, which was meant to support low-income families.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers CHAS eligibility proposal
sections.summary: A speaker proposes evolving the scheme to focus on lower- and middle-income households using CHAS card requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: And then, we went and basically gave it to all households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: So, what I am proposing here is to make use of what we already have, in terms of the CHAS card kind of requirements, such that the scheme from hereon evolves into one focused on where we started out – be focused on the lower-, middle-income households and those who qualify for these additional subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Yes, Mr Chairman, that is what I am trying to ascertain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, is Mr Chua saying, stop the CDC Vouchers and then move over completely to this new scheme?

sections.label: Original CDC Vouchers eligibility uncertainty
sections.summary: A speaker is unsure how the original CDC Vouchers selected eligible Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Whether or not we want to go back to the original CDC Vouchers; I am not sure how exactly did the original CDC Vouchers select the Singaporeans who are eligible.

sections.label: Climate change and green budgeting
sections.summary: Singapore committed to net zero emissions by 2050 and over $10 billion for the Singapore Green Plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is in our interest to support global efforts to deal with climate change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have committed to a target of net zero emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Last month, MOF published an occasional paper explaining how sustainability considerations are factored into various stages of the Government's budgeting cycle.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This includes a commitment of over $10 billion in the decade leading up to FY2030 to support the Singapore Green Plan.

sections.label: Sustainability in government procurement
sections.summary: Environmental sustainability considerations are incorporated into over 60% of government procurement by contract value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Environmental sustainability considerations are already incorporated into over 60% of government procurement by contract value.

sections.label: Tote Board ELI Grant support
sections.summary: Tote Board committed $23 million more to the ELI Grant until FY2028 and is setting up a data hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To support more such partnerships, Tote Board has committed a further $23 million to the ELI Grant until FY2028.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Tote Board will onboard all new projects onto its Impact Measurement Framework by the end of FY2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Tote Board is also collaborating with the National Council of Social Service to set up a data hub to help the social sector move towards evidence-based interventions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The data hub will gather impact evaluation data and provide common standards that more than 500 social service agencies, funders and the Government can use to measure outcomes.

sections.label: HDB state land spot valuations
sections.summary: State land purchased by HDB is valued by spot valuations because HDB is the only buyer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The valuations for state land purchased by HDB are all spot valuations because there is only one buyer – the HDB.

sections.label: Public housing land valuation methodology
sections.summary: Public housing land valuation uses resale flat transactions and site-specific attributes, so fair market value is typically lower than for private housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Hence, for public housing land, the methodology takes into consideration relevant resale flat transactions and site-specific attributes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, for the reasons I have just explained, the fair market value of land sold for public housing will typically be lower than the fair market value of the same land if it were to be sold to a private developer for private housing.

sections.label: HDB housing grants for first-time buyers
sections.summary: HDB provides housing grants to eligible first-time buyers, with lower-income buyers receiving up to $120,000 in support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On top of this, HDB provides housing grants to support eligible first-time buyers, with lower-income buyers receiving more support of up to $120,000.

sections.label: BTO affordability and mortgage servicing
sections.summary: Pricing BTO flats on affordability meant over eight in 10 first-timer families had a mortgage servicing ratio of 25% or lower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: By pricing BTO flats based on affordability, more than eight in 10 first-timer families who collected keys for their BTO flat last year had a mortgage servicing ratio of 25% or lower.

sections.label: HDB flat launch commitment
sections.summary: HDB is on track to exceed its commitment to launch 100,000 new flats from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: HDB is on track to exceed its commitment to launch 100,000 new flats from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: Tender Lite procurement on GeBIZ
sections.summary: Tender Lite covers tenders up to $1 million, with over 700 published on GeBIZ and over 400 awarded as of 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Tender Lite has simplified the procurement of general goods and services, and covers tenders up to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: As of 1 January 2025, more than 700 Tender Lite opportunities have been published on GeBIZ.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Of these, more than 400 have been awarded.

sections.label: Tender Lite launch date
sections.summary: Tender Lite for construction contracts will be launched in May 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Tender Lite for construction contracts will be launched in May 2025.

sections.label: Innovative Procurement Partnership introduction
sections.summary: MOF will introduce the Innovative Procurement Partnership to award contracts covering pilot and subsequent deployment of innovative solutions new to the market.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: To address these concerns, MOF will introduce the Innovative Procurement Partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: This initiative will enable the Government to award contracts covering both pilot and subsequent deployment of innovative solutions which are new to the market.

sections.label: Invoice payment within credit terms
sections.summary: In FY2023, 98% of invoices were paid within their credit terms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: To Ms Jessica Tan's question, in FY2023, 98% of invoices were paid within their credit terms.

sections.label: Faster enquiry turnaround time
sections.summary: The average turnaround time for enquiries is expected to reduce by about 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: This will help them provide more up-to-date and swifter responses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: We expect the average turnaround time for enquiries to reduce by about 30%.

sections.label: Public housing land fair market value
sections.summary: The fair market value for land intended for public housing is typically lower than for private housing because public housing has restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I think what I said was that the fair market value for land intended for public housing is typically lower than the fair market value of land for private housing, because by its nature, public housing has restrictions.

sections.label: Sandbox for creative freelancers
sections.summary: A request was made for a sandbox arrangement where government-commissioned creative projects can hire upskilled local creative freelancers to build their portfolios.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
sentences.text: My point is that without local opportunities for our freelancers to go through upgrading to apply this new knowledge and skills, they will actually be disadvantaged.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
sentences.text: So, my request to the Government is to consider whether we could look at the sandbox arrangement where government-commissioned creative projects can provide a platform for our local creative freelancers who have gone through the upskilling, to be hired and to build their portfolios.

sections.label: PWCS extension decision metrics
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister what metrics will determine whether the PWCS is extended beyond 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: My second clarification is a point I also made in my cut.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: I note the Minister had said that a decision will be made in due course and closer to the time about whether to extend the PWCS beyond 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: As mentioned in my cut, can the Minister share with us what are the metrics used to determine whether or not to exit the programme?

sections.label: PWCS and low-wage workers
sections.summary: The PWCS is aimed at helping employers when they increase the salaries of their low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And these are all different ways in which we will continue to work on with our tripartite partners to look at how we can improve productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But specifically, on the PWCS, this is something that is aimed at helping employers when they increase the salaries of their low-wage workers.

sections.label: PWCS extension decision timing
sections.summary: The decision on whether to extend the PWCS will be made closer to 2026, when the scheme is due to cease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, on the decision to extend or not to extend the PWCS, we will make that decision closer to 2026 when this scheme is due to cease.

sections.label: Entities publish portfolio returns
sections.summary: All entities including Temasek, MAS and GIC publish portfolio returns, but only GIC's asset size stays undisclosed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, first, I want to just reiterate what I said in my main reply earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I said all our entities publish information on their portfolio returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this would include Temasek, MAS and GIC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And then, I also explained that it is only the size of GIC's assets under management that remains undisclosed, because that would then reveal the size of our reserves, and I note that Mr Chua does not disagree with me on that.

sections.label: Assurance Package and GST Vouchers
sections.summary: Targeted assistance includes the Assurance Package and GST Vouchers, with lower-income households and seniors receiving more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: At least, I understand that to be the case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, if those are the two positions, then, when you look at it, that is what we are doing, because for the targeted assistance which we do have, you have the entire Assurance Package and you have GST Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the GST Vouchers, the lower-income households get more and the seniors get more; the middle-income will get, but not as much.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers and CHAS targeting
sections.summary: CDC Vouchers are broad-based, but the suggestion of using CHAS is fair as CDC Vouchers were originally pegged to CHAS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And therefore, you will have some things which are broad-based, like the CDC Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: That said, the suggestion of using CHAS is fair enough, because, as I think Mr Chua knows, when the CDC Vouchers were originally introduced, they were pegged to CHAS as a means of targeting those who had less.

sections.label: Co-funding low-wage worker wage increases
sections.summary: The Government says it is correct to co-fund some cost increases because businesses are asked to support and raise low-wage workers' wages as part of the social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government also believes that because we are asking businesses to support increasing the wages of their low-wage workers and to hire low-wage workers and increase their pay, and that this is an important part of our social compact, that it is correct for us to co-fund some of the cost increases.
